newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 8.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

Indonesia and Malaysia have decided to take the issue of the disputed islands of Sipadan and Ligitan to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. President Suharto met Malaysian Prime Minister Mahatir Mohamad for one and a half hours on Monday in his first state visit to Malaysia since 1993.

Indonesia will look into Dutch media allegations that one of its embassy staff in The Hague is involved with an ecstasy smuggling ring. Last month a Garuda Indonesia pilot was arrested with 8,000 pills of the designer drug strapped to his waist as he boarded a plane bound for Bali.
State oil company Pertamina has signed five contracts with foreign firms for oil and gas exploration and production in Indonesia.

Shares in cigarette manufacturer PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna fell sharply after the market responded negatively to the firm's expansion plans and news of a possible downgrading of its rated debt by Moody's Investor Services.
Six athletes have been accused of doping by Indonesia's National Sports Committee. The athletes are accused of using steroids during last month's national games.
Indonesia and Malaysia plan to work together on the construction of a bridge across the Malacca Straits between the Indonesian island of Sumatra and the peninsula Malaysia.
